earns.answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 2^-} f(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \lim_{x \to 2^-} (x^2 + 1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 5</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 2^+} f(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \lim_{x \to 2^+} (3x - 1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 5</annotation></semantics></math>. Also <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(2) = 5</annotation></semantics></math>. Finds the right one: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{h \to 0^+} \frac{2(1 + h) - 1 - 1}{h}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2</annotation></semantics></math>, and concludes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p'(1) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>

earns.answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 1^-} p(x) = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 1^+} p(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2(1) - 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(1) = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous at 1. From the left, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{h \to 0^-} \frac{(1 + h)^2 - 1}{h}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \lim_{h \to 0^-} (2 + h)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2</annotation></semantics></math>. From the right, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{h \to 0^+} \frac{\left(2(1 + h) - 1\right) - 1}{h}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>h</mi></mrow><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \lim_{h \to 0^+} \frac{2h}{h}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2</annotation></semantics></math>. prompts.title: Where a curve has a vertical tangent
prompts.context: For the curve x2+xy+y2=12x^2 + xy + y^2 = 12, dydx\frac{dy}{dx}=−2x+yx+2y= -\frac{2x + y}{x + 2y}.

Substitutes into the curve: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4y^2 - 2y^2 + y^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3y^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 12</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">±</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \pm 2</annotation></semantics></math>, giving <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-4, 2)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4, -2)</annotation></semantics></math>

Checks the numerator is not 0 at each point: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x + y = -6</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math>

earns.answer: A vertical tangent needs the denominator <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x + 2y = 0</annotation></semantics></math> with the numerator not 0. With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -2y</annotation></semantics></math> the curve gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4y^2 - 2y^2 + y^2 = 12</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^2 = 4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">±</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \pm 2</annotation></semantics></math>. The points are <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-4, 2)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4, -2)</annotation></semantics></math>. prompts.title: Separation with the initial condition
prompts.context: Consider dydx=2xy\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{2x}{y} with y(0)=3y(0) = 3.
prompts.prompt: Find the particular solution y=f(x)y = f(x) with f(0)=3f(0) = 3.
checklist: Separates: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y\,dy = 2x\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>, then antidifferentiates: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{y^2}{2} = x^2 + C</annotation></semantics></math>

Uses the initial condition right away: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{9}{2} = 0 + C</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C = \frac{9}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>

Solves with the positive root, since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0) = 3 > 0</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sqrt{2x^2 + 9}</annotation></semantics></math>

earns.answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y\,dy = 2x\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{y^2}{2} = x^2 + C</annotation></semantics></math>. With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0) = 3</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{9}{2} = C</annotation></semantics></math>. So <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^2 = 2x^2 + 9</annotation></semantics></math>, and since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0) > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sqrt{2x^2 + 9}</annotation></semantics></math>.
earns.why: The constant appears when the antiderivatives are taken and is found from the initial condition before solving for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>; the sign of the root is chosen from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0)</annotation></semantics></math>.

misses.answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{y^2}{2} = x^2</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sqrt{2}\,x</annotation></semantics></math>, and adding <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0) = 3</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sqrt{2}\,x + 3</annotation></semantics></math>.
misses.why: The constant must be added when you antidifferentiate, not after solving for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>. Added at the end, it gives a function that does not solve the equation.

prompts.title: Average value, not average rate

Gets <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>840</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>70</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{840}{12} = 70</annotation></semantics></math> degrees Fahrenheit

checklist: Finds where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> changes sign: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>

Splits the integral there: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^2 (4 - 2t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_2^3 (4 - 2t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -1</annotation></semantics></math>

Adds the sizes: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 + 1 = 5</annotation></semantics></math> meters, which is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^3 |v(t)|\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

earns.answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(t) = 0</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v > 0</annotation></semantics></math> before and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v < 0</annotation></semantics></math> after. Total distance <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \int_0^3 |v(t)|\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \int_0^2 (4 - 2t)\,dt - \int_2^3 (4 - 2t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 4 - (-1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 5</annotation></semantics></math> meters.

misses.answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^3 (4 - 2t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \left[4t - t^2\right]_0^3</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3</annotation></semantics></math> meters.

earns.answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(6)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x(2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>2</mn><mn>6</mn></msubsup><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \int_2^6 v(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 5</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ (-7)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -2</annotation></semantics></math>.

Writes speed as the length of the velocity vector, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{\left(x'(2)\right)^2 + \left(y'(2)\right)^2}</annotation></semantics></math>

Gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>17</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{17}</annotation></semantics></math>, a magnitude, with no use of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math>

prompts.title: Toward the origin when r is negative

Tests <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 5</annotation></semantics></math> on its own: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum \frac{1}{n}</annotation></semantics></math>, the harmonic series, diverges

Tests <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -1</annotation></semantics></math> on its own: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum \frac{(-1)^n}{n}</annotation></semantics></math> converges by the alternating series test, and gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1, 5)</annotation></semantics></math>

earns.answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{n \to \infty} \left|\frac{(x - 2)^{n+1}}{(n + 1)3^{n+1}}\cdot\frac{n\cdot 3^n}{(x - 2)^n}\right|</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{|x - 2|}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is less than 1 when <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo><</mo><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1 < x < 5</annotation></semantics></math>.
